Convert matches, entities or noun phrases to a quanteda index

Source: R/as_index.R
as_index.Rd

Turn the positions that spacy_match(), spacy_extract_entity() or spacy_extract_nounphrases() return into an index of quanteda, as quanteda::index() makes, so that quanteda::kwic() can show each of them in its context. Making the index needs neither quanteda nor spaCy.

Usage

as_index(x)

Arguments

x

the output of spacy_match(), spacy_extract_entity() or spacy_extract_nounphrases(): a data.frame with the columns doc_id, start_id and length. It can also be NULL, which spacy_extract_entity() and spacy_extract_nounphrases() return when they find nothing, and which gives an index with no rows.

Value

An object of class index, as quanteda::index() returns: a data.frame with one row for each row of x, in the same order, and the columns

  • docname the document, from doc_id, in Unicode's composed form (NFC), as the details describe;

  • from and to the positions of the first and last token, from start_id and length;

  • pattern a factor: the label of a match, the ent_type of an entity, or "nounphrase" for a noun phrase.

Details

The positions count spaCy's tokens from 1 in each document, with its tokens of whitespace. They are the positions in quanteda::as.tokens(spacy_parse(x)) for the same texts and the same pipeline, and not those in quanteda::tokens(x), which are quanteda's tokens, or in the output of spacy_tokenize(), which by default leaves out whitespace. So give quanteda::kwic() the tokens of spacy_parse(), as in the examples. quanteda::kwic() does not check that an index was made from the tokens it is given: with other tokens, it shows whatever is at those positions.

spacy_parse() needs the sentences of each document, which come from the parser of the language model or from a sentence segmenter. In a pipeline that sets no sentence boundaries, spacy_match() still returns the positions of its matches, but spacy_parse() fails, and so cannot give the tokens for a concordance.

quanteda keeps the names of documents in Unicode's composed form (NFC), so that an "e" followed by a combining accent becomes the single accented character. as_index() does the same to doc_id when the stringi package is installed, which quanteda needs: the matches of a document whose name is not in that form then keep their place in the concordance, which would otherwise drop them without a message. Giving the same quanteda::corpus() to spacy_match() and to spacy_parse() has the same effect, since the names in a corpus are already in that form.

A match of a dependency pattern has one row for each of its nodes, and so one row in the index for each node, also when two nodes are the same token. quanteda::kwic() keeps the rows of the index in their order, and drops those of documents that the tokens do not have. When the tokens have every document, row i of the concordance is row i of x, so the other columns of x, such as match_id and node, can be added to it.

The concordance shows the matches that it is given. Which matches spacy_match() returns where they overlap is set by its overlap, whose rule is not that of quanteda::kwic(x, pattern), as the details of spacy_match() describe. A concordance of matches keeps a "New York" inside another label's "New York Times", for instance, which quanteda's own search for the two would drop.

See also

spacy_match(), spacy_extract_entity(), spacy_extract_nounphrases(), quanteda::kwic()

Examples

# an index needs no spaCy: here, of matches written by hand
m <- data.frame(doc_id = c("d1", "d1"), label = c("city", "paper"),
                start_id = c(2, 2), length = c(2, 3))
as_index(m)
#>   docname from to pattern
#> 1      d1    2  3    city
#> 2      d1    2  4   paper
as_index(NULL)
#> [1] docname from    to      pattern
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
spacy_initialize()
txt <- c(d1 = "The New York Times is a paper in New York.",
         d2 = "Jane Smith wrote the book in Boston.")
toks <- quanteda::as.tokens(spacy_parse(txt))

# matches in context
m <- spacy_match(txt, quanteda::phrase(c("new york", "the book")))
quanteda::kwic(toks, index = as_index(m), window = 3)

# entities and noun phrases
quanteda::kwic(toks, index = as_index(spacy_extract_entity(txt)), window = 3)
quanteda::kwic(toks, index = as_index(spacy_extract_nounphrases(txt)),
               window = 3)
spacy_finalize()
} # }
